messages:
Linda (PM): quick sync — we need to finalize auth + tenant scoping for the next API surface PRD. customers worry about key rotation impact on long-lived chat/websocket sessions. thoughts?
Ajay (Eng): agree. main tradeoff: short TTL keys are safer but break long-lived SSE/WebSocket sessions. we should support key rotation with 'session tokens' for flows that need long life.
Kevin (Security): +1. propose model: API keys (kid + secret) for issuing short-lived session tokens (JWT with exp), signed by platform. rotation rotates signing key and marks old API keys revoked.
Maria (DevEx): note: dev experience needs a clear migration story. customers will expect an opt-in header for project-scoped requests like `x-rw-project-id`. also easy curl examples.
Sam (Platform): implementation concerns: for streaming/ws we can allow a session JWT presented during the ws handshake and validate on reconnect. need to decide whether to accept both API key and session token during dual-accept window.
Ajay (Eng): implementation sketch:
```
POST /v1/sessions
Authorization: Bearer API_KEY_KID
{ "project_id": "proj_123", "scopes": ["chat","embeddings"] }
=> returns { "session_token": "jwt...", "expires_in": 86400 }
```
The session_token is what clients use for streaming and function calls.
Kevin (Security): must include `kid` in JWT header so we can rotate signing keys. revoke list lookup on every reconnect. also rate-limit issuing endpoints.
Maria (DevEx): docs note: curl + node examples for obtaining session token, using it for streaming and for function/tool-calling. show what breaks when key rotated.
Linda (PM): launch criteria suggestion: 1) API supports session token issuance + validation; 2) dual-accept for old API keys for 90 days; 3) migration guide + sample code; 4) automated audit logs for rotation events; 5) e2e tests for ws reconnect and active tool calls during rotation.
Sam (Platform): rollouts: gradual by org. start with internal orgs, then beta customers, then GA. feature flag gating per-tenant.
Ajay (Eng): corner cases: embeddings pipeline — many batch jobs use API keys in CI. they will need to be swapped for service tokens or long-lived project tokens. we should support project-scoped long-lived tokens with restricted scopes (embeddings-only).
Kevin (Security): also consider tooling/function calling risk: tool invocations run in tenant context. ensure token encodes project/org id and we enforce per-project policies server-side. no trusting client-supplied project_id without token binding.
Maria (DevEx): flagging UX friction: customers with infra-as-code will want key rotation CLI. we should expose `rwctl keys rotate --project proj_123 --grace 30d` example.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: auth/session-service -> canary at 2026-05-02T03:00Z.
audit-bot: log: rotation-schedule created by Kevin (Security) for signer_k23, grace=90d.
Linda (PM): decision points for next week sync: a) support both session tokens + project-scoped long-lived tokens? b) dual-accept window length? c) headers vs body param for project scoping? please reply with votes and short rationale.
Ajay (Eng): vote: both token types. rationale: gives flexibility for CI (long-lived) and client apps (session tokens).
Kevin (Security): vote: both. dual-accept: 90 days max. header for project scoping (x-rw-project-id) + require binding in token for trust.
Maria (DevEx): vote: header + examples. make default SDK behavior to exchange API key for session token automatically.
Sam (Platform): vote: both tokens + feature-flagged per-org. we'll need metrics: sessions_issued, failed_reauth, rotation_failures.
Linda (PM): great. I'll draft the PRD with launch criteria and migration plan and share before Friday. thanks all :thumbsup:
